chunks: 5586 - And in the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, he said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who gave charity to his son in the form of wealth or a house: does he have the right to return to it? He said: "Yes, unless he is a minor."

key_terms.الدَّارِ: a house or residence given as property
key_terms.اِبْنِهِ: his son, indicating the family relationship central to the ruling
key_terms.بِالْمَالِ: in the form of wealth or property
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ: gave as charity or a charitable gift
key_terms.صَغِيرًا: a minor child, whose status creates an exception to the ruling
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ فِيهِ: to take it back or revoke the transfer

ai.seo_question: Can a father take back property or wealth he gave to his son?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a father who has transferred property to his son as a charitable gift. It indicates that he may revoke it, except in the case where the son is a minor, highlighting a distinction in legal treatment based on the child’s status.
